src/routes/cardsRouter.ts: each route follows the form `cardsRouter.post("/create", apiKeyValidator, bodySchemaValidator(createCardSchema), create)`, using the shared middleware and schema abstractions
src/routes/statementsRouter.ts: uses the same pattern, e.g. `statementsRouter.post("/recharge", apiKeyValidator, bodySchemaValidator(rechargeSchema), recharge)`

parsedVerdict.reasoning: The src/routes module covers a single concern: HTTP route wiring. cardsRouter.ts and statementsRouter.ts each build an express Router whose routes all follow the same pattern: optional apiKeyValidator, then bodySchemaValidator(schema), then a controller handler. router.ts only combines the two sub-routers. All three files use the same abstractions (express Router, the shared middlewares, schemas from src/schemas), and no file bypasses them. No rule or invariant is defined twice. Validation lives in shared schemas and middleware, and reusing blockCardSchema for /block and /unblock is reuse, not duplication. Two small points do not amount to a failure. First, statementsRouter.ts imports getStatement from cardsController, so its grouping is a little loose. Second, apiKeyValidator runs on only some routes, which matches a deliberate split between company-authenticated and cardholder routes. Neither point breaks the module's cohesion.
